## Dashboard analytics (`/dashboard/analytics`)

The requested date range determines the granularity of the response:

- **30 days or less:** The endpoint returns raw data points.
- **More than 30 days:** The server returns daily aggregates instead of raw data points. These responses do not include intraday detail.

Use the optional `max_points` query parameter to limit the number of data points returned and control response size. It does not change the date-range rule for aggregation.

arguments.notes:
Investigation — dispute_509 / order_409. Evidence completeness (§F.1): Checked the dispute record and the evidence system, and read the only submitted file, buyer_103’s evidence_709 (submitted 2024-01-18T10:00:00Z), including all four attachments and the buyer narrative. No separate evidence file was submitted by seller_205. Reviewed seller listing_309 and both parties’ statements in thread_609. The listing advertises a 1999 1st Edition Base Set Charizard #4, PSA 7 NM, cert 45678902, with an intact holder, minor centering issues and light edge wear. The seller states the holder is untampered and argues PSA grades on multiple factors and accounts for print lines; these arguments are not independent verification.

Buyer evidence — evidence_709: All four attachments are marked verified by the evidence system. The platform-generated descriptions identify (1) a full front view in a PSA holder labeled PSA 7; (2) a measurement overlay showing approximately 65/35 left/right and 55/45 top/bottom, with the description noting that centering exceeding 60/40 typically limits the grade to 6; (3) a close-up showing a horizontal print line through the middle of the card, visible through the holder; and (4) a screenshot of PSA’s grading guide quoting the PSA 7 description of slight surface wear visible upon close inspection. The screenshot is a reference, not an independent appraisal. The buyer’s proposed grade cap and suspicion of tampering or grading error are party assertions, not verified findings.

Platform verification (§3.6 Level 1): The grading_company_api certification_verification at 2024-01-18T09:00:00Z returned PSA cert 45678902 as valid for “1999 Pokemon Base Set Charizard 1st Edition #4,” grade PSA 7, issue date 2023-11-15, holder_integrity: verified. This matches the listing and provides no support for certification failure or holder tampering. The lookup confirms the recorded grade and holder integrity; it does not independently regrade the photographed card or evaluate the specific defects. Under §3.6, the listing and message history are Level 2 records, the submitted photos and screenshot are Level 4 evidence, and party interpretations are Level 5. Hi Alice,

I recommend protecting the two TechCorp engineering FTEs listed in each joint roadmap. Prioritize InnovateTech for proactive release engineering. Keep GlobalSoft in a stable maintenance posture for the live integration, but reserve delivery capacity within its planned allocation for the enterprise rollout. Neither Q4 update reports incident response or resolution times, so the uptime figures don’t establish SLA attainment.

InnovateTech — proactive engineering investment
• Support runbook SLA (response / resolution target): P1 1 hour / 4 hours; P2 4 hours / 24 hours; P3 8 hours / 72 hours; P4 24 hours / 1 week.
• Q4 update (James Wilson, Jan. 12): $125,000 revenue share; 847 support tickets resolved; 94% customer satisfaction; 99.97% API uptime.
• Q1 joint roadmap: January — API v2.0 integration kickoff, security audit completion, and documentation update. February — beta testing with select customers, joint marketing materials, and partner certification program launch. March — GA release, co-branded webinar, and success metrics review. Planned engineering: 3 InnovateTech FTE and 2 TechCorp FTE. Q1 targets: 500 customers by quarter-end, >90% customer satisfaction, and 30% support ticket reduction.
• Allocation recommendation: Protect the two TechCorp FTEs for API v2.0 integration, security audit follow-through, and beta-to-GA readiness rather than treating this as maintenance-only. Reassess incremental capacity if the audit or beta puts March GA at risk.

GlobalSoft — stable production maintenance, with planned Q1 delivery capacity
• Support runbook SLA (response / resolution target): P1 30 min / 2 hours; P2 2 hours / 12 hours; P3 4 hours / 48 hours; P4 12 hours / 5 days.
• Q4 update (Nina Patel, Jan. 12): $198,000 revenue share; 1,203 support tickets resolved; 96% customer satisfaction; 99.99% API uptime.
• Q1 joint roadmap: January — enterprise SSO integration, performance optimization sprint, and customer migration planning. February — large customer pilot, joint case study development, and training program launch. March — full enterprise rollout, partnership expansion discussion, and Q1 retrospective. Planned engineering: 4 GlobalSoft FTE and 2 TechCorp FTE. Q1 targets: 50 enterprise accounts, 25% QoQ revenue growth, and +10 points in NPS.
• Allocation recommendation: GlobalSoft’s higher reported uptime and satisfaction support maintaining the existing production support posture, not adding headcount now. Reserve time within the two planned TechCorp FTEs for SSO, performance work, and migration readiness. Revisit staffing if the pilot exposes rollout risks or support demand threatens coverage against the tighter SLA targets.
arguments.subject: Q1 engineering allocation: InnovateTech vs. GlobalSoft

final:
I reviewed both partners’ support runbooks, Q4 update emails, and joint roadmaps, then sent Alice Wong an engineering allocation summary comparing their SLA commitments, Q4 performance, and Q1 milestones.

- **InnovateTech:** Prioritize proactive engineering within the two planned TechCorp FTEs for API v2.0 integration, security audit follow-through, and the March general-availability release.
- **GlobalSoft:** Maintain the current production support posture without adding headcount, while reserving capacity within its two planned TechCorp FTEs for enterprise SSO, performance work, and migration readiness.

The email also notes that neither Q4 update reported incident response or resolution times, so the reported uptime figures don’t establish whether either partner met its support SLAs.

InnovateTech — proactive engineering investment
• SLA commitments (InnovateTech support runbook; response / resolution target): P1 1 hour / 4 hours; P2 4 hours / 24 hours; P3 8 hours / 72 hours; P4 24 hours / 1 week.
• Q4 performance (James Wilson’s Jan. 12 update): $125,000 revenue share, 847 support tickets resolved, 94% customer satisfaction, and 99.97% API uptime.
• Q1 commitments (InnovateTech joint roadmap): January — API v2.0 kickoff, security audit completion, and documentation update. February — select-customer beta, joint marketing materials, and partner certification launch. March — GA release, co-branded webinar, and success metrics review. The roadmap lists 3 InnovateTech engineering FTE and 2 TechCorp engineering FTE, with targets of 500 adopting customers by quarter-end, >90% satisfaction, and 30% fewer support tickets.

Hi Bob,

Here’s a comparison of CloudServices and DataPlatform based on their proposal emails and integration notes. DataPlatform’s base quote is $13,000/year lower and its proposed rollout is two weeks shorter. CloudServices quotes a higher uptime SLA and includes 24/7 dedicated support. The prices aren’t directly comparable until we know what DataPlatform’s premium support costs and what it covers.

CloudServices — $85,000/year all-inclusive; 99.99% uptime SLA; 24/7 dedicated support. The proposed 11-week rollout includes 2 weeks of discovery, 6 of implementation, 2 of testing, and 1 for go-live. The architecture uses an AWS Application Load Balancer, Amazon EKS with managed node groups, Aurora PostgreSQL with read replicas, and ElastiCache for Redis. This is the more natural fit if the workload needs relational queries or already runs on PostgreSQL. The vendor reports AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, SOC 2 Type II, and GDPR-compliant data handling. Open items include identity provider, data retention, and disaster recovery targets (RTO/RPO).

CloudServices documentation (from its integration notes):
- Compliance & Certifications: https://cloudservices.com/compliance/certifications
- Security Whitepaper: https://cloudservices.com/security/whitepaper
- SOC 2 Report Request: https://cloudservices.com/compliance/soc2-request

DataPlatform — $72,000/year base; 99.9% uptime SLA with credits; business-hours support with a premium upgrade available. The proposed 9-week rollout includes 1 week of discovery, 5 of implementation, 2 of testing, and 1 for go-live. The serverless-first architecture uses a managed API gateway with rate limiting, Lambda with provisioned concurrency, DynamoDB global tables, and DAX caching. It reduces the need to manage container infrastructure, but we should validate that our query patterns fit DynamoDB before assuming the shorter migration is achievable. The vendor reports encryption at rest and in transit, SOC 2 Type II, regular penetration testing, and HIPAA-compliant options. Open items include query patterns, multi-region requirements, and required certifications.

DataPlatform documentation (from its integration notes):
- Trust & Compliance Center: https://dataplatform.com/trust/compliance
- Security Overview: https://dataplatform.com/security
- SOC 2 Report: https://dataplatform.com/trust/soc2

Before choosing, I’d ask DataPlatform for a quote with comparable support and confirm SLA scope, exclusions, and remedies with both vendors. We should also verify that each vendor’s compliance evidence covers the services and configuration it’s proposing.

# Acme Corp Account Status

**Contract:** Enterprise Premium, with an annual contract value of **$240,000**. The project status document lists David Kim as account manager and September 2025 as the renewal date.

**Client concerns and priorities:**
- Large analytics reports (10,000+ rows) load slowly. Acme wants this addressed before its planned February 1 executive rollout. Advanced analytics with deeper drill-downs is its top feature priority; the project status lists January 31 as the target for general availability.
- Acme needs pricing clarity for additional business units it plans to onboard in Q2.
- Field teams want better offline support and faster mobile load times. Acme also requested prebuilt dashboard templates for Sales, Marketing, and Operations.

**Positive feedback:** Acme reported a noticeably faster dashboard and a smooth Okta SSO rollout.

Sources: *Project Status - Acme Corp* (Jan 13, 2025) for contract and project details; *Client Notes - Acme Corp* (Jan 14, 2025) for feedback, concerns, and client priorities.

Hi David,

Please review the tracker-based priorities below and sign off on what we can commit to next sprint before confirming commitments separately with each client. The priorities reflect Engineering’s assessed severity, not client-reported urgency. No client-raised issue in the tracker meets P0 or P1.

P2: Beta Inc - Bulk exports above ~50K records fail intermittently (ENG-412): reproduced in 6 of 40 attempts; chunked or async exports succeeded every time the single-pass export failed.
P2: Acme Corp - Analytics reports above ~10K rows take more than 8 seconds to render (ENG-418); smaller reports render normally and the page remains functional.
P3: Beta Inc - Reported webhook drops during high-traffic windows (ENG-421) are low severity and unconfirmed: no drops across 5,000 test events, including simulated high traffic. Keep monitoring and hold pending further evidence.

The following requests and concerns have no severity assessment in the tracker and were not assigned sprint priorities:
• Acme Corp: advanced analytics drill-downs, better mobile offline support and load times, department-specific dashboard templates, and pricing for additional business units.
• Beta Inc: guaranteed or at-least-once webhook delivery (separate from the reported drops), multi-tenant workspaces, clarity on pricing changes, and a dedicated engineering escalation channel.

Thanks

arguments.body:
Hi James and Nina,

Here’s a combined summary of the planned Q1 2025 milestones from the InnovateTech and GlobalSoft joint roadmaps for the Quarterly Partner Review.

January
- InnovateTech: Kick off the API v2.0 integration, complete the security audit, and update the documentation.
- GlobalSoft: Integrate enterprise SSO, run the performance optimization sprint, and plan customer migration.

February
- InnovateTech: Run beta testing with select customers, prepare joint marketing materials, and launch the partner certification program.
- GlobalSoft: Run the large-customer pilot, develop a joint case study, and launch the training program.

March
- InnovateTech: Release the integrated solution for general availability, hold a co-branded webinar, and review success metrics.
- GlobalSoft: Complete the full enterprise rollout, discuss expanding the partnership, and hold the Q1 retrospective.

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the feedback. I’m glad the API performance improvements are noticeable and the new authentication flow is smoother.

The bulk export fix for the intermittent timeouts is about 80% complete and is still in progress this sprint (Jan 6–19). We don’t have a confirmed release date yet.

Custom webhook support is about 70% complete. We’re still targeting Jan 25 for general availability, but that date is at risk because testing is on hold until the Beta Inc staging environment is available.

We’ll schedule a call to discuss the roadmap and your concerns about how the pricing tier changes could affect your budget. I’ll follow up with some times.

Best,
Sarah

I confirmed we’ll schedule the roadmap and pricing call and follow up with proposed times. No calendar invite was sent.
